claims.text: Point-wise dependencies between input and decision can be estimated on the fly with a single inference without access to token logits using a non-parametric uncertainty quantification method.
The proposed non-parametric uncertainty estimator informs the statistical interpretation of decision trustworthiness.
A decision-making agent design can generate actions based on user prompts.
The decision-making agent solicits user preferences when more than one action exhibits high estimated point-wise dependencies.

evidence.description: The authors introduce a non-parametric uncertainty quantification method that efficiently estimates input-decision point-wise dependencies in a single inference with no token logit access.
The paper states that the point-wise dependency estimator informs statistical interpretations regarding how trustworthy a decision is.
The paper describes an agent design capable of mapping user prompts like 'take a bath' to specific actions like 'turn on the bathroom light'.
The agent design prompts users to clarify preferences whenever multiple potential actions yield high point-wise dependencies.

methodologies.name: Non-parametric Uncertainty Quantification Estimator
methodologies.description: Estimates point-wise dependencies between input and decision on the fly using a single inference pass without relying on token logits.

methodologies.name: Preference-Guided Decision-Making Agent Architecture
methodologies.description: Generates step-by-step plan actions from user prompts and requests user intervention/preferences when uncertainty/point-wise dependency is ambiguous across multiple actions.

limitations.text: Existing approaches for uncertainty estimation in LLMs are either white-box or computationally demanding, limiting their deployment with black-box proprietary LLMs within strict budgets.
